scenes.heading: Invalidating from Author or Publish
scenes.narration: Dispatcher. Invalidating from Author or Publish. In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What does the standard Dispatcher Flush agent do when it is configured on Author?
scenes.heading: On Author, the standard Dispatcher Flush agent sends an invalidation request when a page is activated
scenes.body: The speech says the standard Dispatcher Flush agent is installed by default and, when configured on Author, sends an invalidation request to Dispatcher when a page is activated.

scenes.question: Where should the Transport URI of a standard Dispatcher Flush agent point?
scenes.heading: The Transport URI should point to /dispatcher/invalidate.cache on the Dispatcher host
scenes.body: The speech says the flush agent's Transport URI points to /dispatcher/invalidate.cache on the Dispatcher host.

scenes.question: When is the flush agent's URI property used to target a specific farm?
scenes.heading: The URI property is used only with path-based virtual hosts to target a specific farm
scenes.body: The speech states that the URI property is used only with path-based virtual hosts, to target a specific farm.

scenes.question: What is the recommended credential practice for Dispatcher Flush agents?
scenes.heading: If credentials are used, create a dedicated replication user instead of using admin
scenes.body: The source says the agent does not need a user name and password, but if they are set they are sent with basic authentication, and it recommends creating a dedicated user instead of using admin.

scenes.question: Why can invalidating Dispatcher directly from Author be difficult in some network topologies?
scenes.heading: Author-side invalidation can fail because Dispatcher must be reachable from the Author instance
scenes.body: The speech lists reachability as one of the two issues with invalidating from Author: Dispatcher must be reachable from the Author instance, which a firewall may block.

scenes.question: What race condition can occur when invalidation and publication happen at the same time?
scenes.heading: Dispatcher can cache the old page again if a user requests it after invalidation but before the new publication arrives
scenes.body: The speech explains that publication and invalidation happen at the same time, so a user can request the page after it is removed from cache but before the new page is published, leading Dispatcher to cache the old page again.

scenes.question: What changes when cache invalidation is moved from Author to Publish?
scenes.heading: With publish-side invalidation, each Publish instance sends the invalidation request when it receives the published page
scenes.body: The speech says invalidating from the publish instance moves cache management to Publish: the publish instance sends the invalidation request when it receives a published page. It also notes the agent must be configured on every affected Publish instance.

scenes.heading: Quick recap
items: On Author, the standard Dispatcher Flush agent sends an invalidation request when a page is activated
The Transport URI should point to /dispatcher/invalidate.cache on the Dispatcher host
The URI property is used only with path-based virtual hosts to target a specific farm
If credentials are used, create a dedicated replication user instead of using admin
Author-side invalidation can fail because Dispatcher must be reachable from the Author instance
Dispatcher can cache the old page again if a user requests it after invalidation but before the new publication arrives
With publish-side invalidation, each Publish instance sends the invalidation request when it receives the published page
